message.reasoning:
I'm planning comprehensive JUnit 4 tests for CSVFormat, covering factory methods, predefined formats, validation, equals/hashCode, and the parse/print/format methods to maximize branch coverage.

For validate(), I need to test the various IllegalArgumentException cases: delimiter matching quote character, escape character, or comment marker, and delimiter being a line break character. I also want to check the QuoteMode enum values and structure the test file with many focused test methods covering each withXxx() setter and its validation logic.

For equals(), I need thorough coverage comparing every field pairwise - same object, null, different class, and then each field (delimiter, quoteMode, quoteCharacter, commentMarker, escapeCharacter, nullString, header, ignoreSurroundingSpaces, ignoreEmptyLines, skipHeaderRecord, recordSeparator) in both null and non-null mismatched states before confirming full equality.

I also plan to test hashCode() for basic consistency, format() for a sanity check, and the getters against their default values, along with the isXxxSet() boolean methods checking both true and false branches.

For the print methods, I need cases covering null values with and without nullString, quoteMode ALL behavior, CharSequence vs non-CharSequence objects, trim flag variations, newRecord delimiter handling, and the branching logic between plain append, escape, and quote handling - plus dedicated tests for printAndEscape (delimiter, CR, LF, escape char) and printAndQuote covering all quote scenarios.

Beyond that I still need coverage for println's trailing delimiter and record separator variants, printRecord with multiple values, toString/toStringArray behavior with null elements and header comments, trim() for both String and non-String CharSequence types, and one test per with* method to confirm each produces a correctly modified CSVFormat. Time to start writing out the actual test code now.

Planning test method names for QuoteMode's valueOf/Predefined behavior, constructor validation around delimiter/escape/quote/comment characters rejecting line breaks or nulls appropriately, and validate() throwing when quote char equals delimiter.

I'm continuing to list out test names covering validation edge cases (duplicate headers, escape/quote-mode conflicts) plus the various withHeader overloads including variadic, enum, and mocked ResultSet/ResultSetMetaData cases, along with tests for the remaining builder methods like withQuoteMode, withRecordSeparator, withTrim, and withAllowMissingColumnNames.

Now I'm planning tests for equals() covering same instance, null, different class, and mismatches across every field (delimiter, quote mode, quote char, comment marker, escape char, null string, header, surrounding spaces, empty lines, skip header record, record separator), plus a fully-equal case, followed by hashCode consistency tests, basic format tests, getter defaults, and the isXSet boolean checks, and finally parse/print tests including printing to an Appendable, stdout, and a File.

I'm continuing the print-related tests: printing to a Path, then covering printObject behavior across null values with and without null string configuration under different quote modes, non-null CharSequence and non-CharSequence values, trimming, and delimiter appending for non-new records. I'm also planning escape-character printing without quoting, and an extensive set of quote-mode tests covering ALL, ALL_NON_NULL, NON_NUMERIC (numeric and non-numeric), NONE, and MINIMAL mode across various edge cases like empty records, special characters, comment markers, delimiters, quote characters, trailing spaces, and cases needing no quoting at all.

Since trim(), toStringArray(), and printAndEscape/printAndQuote are private, I recognize I can only exercise them indirectly through the public print API, which is fine for branch coverage purposes. To hit the trim() branch for a non-String CharSequence, I need to pass a StringBuilder as the value with trim enabled, since the code checks if the value is a CharSequence and calls the private trim method on it when trimming is requested.

I'm planning to call CSVFormat.DEFAULT.withTrim(true).print() directly with a StringBuilder containing padded text and verify the output comes out trimmed, since print(Object, Appendable, boolean) is public. For header duplicate validation, I'll construct withHeader("a","a") to trigger the validate() method that should throw. I'll also use Mockito to mock ResultSet and ResultSetMetaData since mockito-all is available, and I'll import QuoteMode assuming its enum constants are ALL, ALL_NON_NULL, NON_NUMERIC, NONE, and MINIMAL based on how they're used elsewhere, using literal characters instead of importing the Constants class where possible.

Now I'm assembling the full compilable test file, making sure to cover withAllowMissingColumnNames() behavior on EXCEL's predefined format, and to test Predefined.valueOf along with getFormat() results. I also want to add checks for the MYSQL, POSTGRESQL_CSV, POSTGRESQL_TEXT, INFORMIX_UNLOAD, INFORMIX_UNLOAD_CSV, and TDF predefined formats, asserting at least some of their key fields.

I'm working out a test to confirm that calling newFormat(',').withQuoteMode(QuoteMode.NONE) throws an IllegalArgumentException, since newFormat leaves escape null while QuoteMode.NONE requires an escape character, so the constructor's validate() call should fail immediately — writing the corresponding @Test(expected = IllegalArgumentException.class) case now.

Adding more validation tests...

Adding line break validation tests...

Then testing newFormat with a valid delimiter, checking that all the other fields default to null or false.

Now I'm writing tests for valueOf, verifying "Default" resolves to CSVFormat.DEFAULT and invalid strings throw exceptions, then starting on equals tests covering various field comparisons.

Now I should test the isXxxSet getter methods, checking that isCommentMarkerSet and isEscapeCharacterSet correctly return false by default and true after setting those values.

Then I add tests for null string and quote character detection, followed by format() tests checking basic joining and escaping of special characters like commas, and I'm starting to draft a parse() test to verify round-trip parsing behavior.

Adding print method tests...

Actually closing that printer could close System.out itself since it wraps that stream, which might break later tests trying to write output. I should avoid calling close() there and just verify the printer isn't null instead.

Now I'm turning to the print(Object, Appendable, boolean) method, checking how null values behave when there's no nullString set—since DEFAULT format still has a quote character configured, the null case appends an empty string rather than throwing.

So it outputs "hi" unquoted directly, matching my expectation. Now I need to check whether trim gets applied to the StringBuilder input — since it's a CharSequence, trim() checks if it's specifically a String type before doing anything special.

Since it isn't a String, trim falls through to manual position/length logic, which is exactly the branch I want to test. So I'll write a test where trim is true and the value is a plain String to hit that other branch, plus a test verifying printAndEscape correctly escapes delimiters, newlines, carriage returns, and the escape character itself when using an escape-enabled, unquoted format.

Tracing through the escaping logic character by character on "a,b\nc\rd\\e" confirms each special character triggers a flush of the preceding segment plus the escaped character, with LF and CR converted to 'n' and 'r' respectively while the escape character is written as-is—matching the expected output "a\\,b\\nc\\rd\\\\e".

So putting it all together, the final literal string is "a\,b\nc\rd\\e", which as a Java string literal I'd need to write as "a\\,b\\nc\\rd\\\\e" to assert correctly.

Continuing through the "d" and "e" segments, the escaped backslash itself becomes two literal backslashes, giving the final expected string "a\\,b\\nc\\rd\\\\e" which matches my earlier derivation. Now I'm moving on to testing the printAndQuote method with different quote character configurations and quote modes.

Finishing the test assertion...

I confirm that since newRecord is false, only the second condition applies -- checking whether '!' (0x21) falls at or below the comment character '#' (0x23), which it does, so the quoting behavior matches my expected output.

I don't have direct access to Constants.COMMENT's value in the test since it's a private import, so I'm reasoning it out logically -- it's almost certainly '#' based on how Apache Commons CSV defines things. To make the test more robust against that assumption, I could instead use a space character (0x20) as the input, since that's guaranteed to be less than or equal to COMMENT regardless of its exact value, as long as COMMENT sits at or above 0x20.

I'm writing a test case that prints a value starting with a space when newRecord is false, expecting the quote logic to trigger and wrap the output in quotes, while noting the assumption about COMMENT's value in a comment.

Then I'm adding another test where the value contains a delimiter mid-string ("abc,def"), tracing through the logic to confirm the first character doesn't hit any special-case branches, so execution falls into the scanning loop that checks each character for line breaks, quote chars, or delimiters.

I'm also adding a test for a value containing the quote character mid-string ("abc\"def"), expecting the output to wrap the value in quotes and double the embedded quote character, then tracing how quote=true gets set once the scan hits the quote char position.

Right, the loop breaks without incrementing pos, so pos stays at 3 when quote is detected. Since quote is true, the code skips the end-check block and exits the switch case for MINIMAL mode.

Now with quote=true, it appends the opening quote character to output, then re-scans from the beginning: it walks through the string, and whenever it hits an embedded quote character it appends everything up to and including that character (doubling the quote for escaping) and resets the start marker, tracing through "abc\"def" character by character to build the properly escaped quoted output.

So the resulting quoted string doubles the inner quote, giving "abc""def" as the final output, matching my expected assertion. Now I'm setting up the next test case for MINIMAL mode where a trailing space at the end of the input should also trigger quoting.

I write a test with input "abc " and trace through the logic: the scan finds no special characters, but afterward checks the last character, sees it's a space (0x20), and since that's <= SP, it sets quote=true even though no delimiter was found mid-string. Then I trace through the quoting/escaping loop appending characters up to the space at the end.

I move on to a simpler test case, testPrintAndQuote_modeMINIMAL_noQuoteNeeded, checking that a plain value with no special characters and no trailing space prints unquoted. I note that the earlier tests using default newFormat already exercise the null quoteMode-treated-as-minimal branch.

Then I write tests for println(): verifying that with trailingDelimiter true and a record separator set, it outputs the delimiter plus separator, while with trailingDelimiter false and no separator it outputs nothing. Next I write printRecord() tests, confirming multiple values join with commas and a trailing separator, and starting a case for empty values.

Now moving to toString() tests, checking that DEFAULT format's string representation includes delimiter, quote char, record separator, and skip-header-record info, and that a fully customized format with escape char, comment marker, null string, and other options reflects those settings correctly in its string output.

I'm double-checking DEFAULT's actual constructor parameters to verify default values for ignoreSurroundingSpaces and ignoreEmptyLines, since these affect what toString() should output.

I want to add an assertion checking that "EmptyLines:ignored" appears in the default format's toString output, and confirm surrounding spaces aren't marked ignored by default. I also need to be careful testing for absence of "Header:" since "HeaderComments:" contains that same substring, which could cause a false assertion.

Writing predefined format tests...

Adding more test cases...

Adding more test cases to verify header and header comments arrays return defensive clones rather than internal references.

Adding tests for withQuote char overload... Now I'm assembling everything into one file, checking for duplicate method names and verifying compile correctness, including confirming DEFAULT's escape is null so withCommentMarker works fine.

I'm tracing through the validation logic for the test where quote and comment marker are both set to '#' on a format with null escape and comment initially, confirming that withQuote('#') alone passes validation since delimiter, escape, and quote mode don't conflict, then checking what happens when withCommentMarker('#') is chained afterward.

For that case, since the quote character equals the comment marker ('#' equals '#'), the validation throws as expected. Now I'm tracing the escape-equals-comment test similarly: withEscape('#') on a comma-delimited format passes since there's no comment marker yet, then chaining withCommentMarker('#') sets both escape and comment to '#', and I'm checking each validation branch—delimiter mismatches are all fine, quote is null so that check skips—looking for where the escape-equals-comment condition triggers the throw.

I confirm the logic works correctly for these cases, then move to verifying the escape-equals-delimiter and quote-equals-delimiter tests, tracing through how withEscape and withQuote construct new format instances that ultimately fail validation when the character matches the delimiter.

Now I check the null header and empty header varargs cases: passing null keeps header null and skips duplicate checks, while calling withHeader() with no arguments produces an empty array rather than null, so validation just iterates over nothing.

Then I trace through withHeader for enum classes, ResultSets, and their metadata variants, confirming that each null case cascades down to withHeader((String[]) null), leaving header null and getHeader() returning null as expected.

Now I check the mockito imports for mock and when are correctly included, then double-check the file compiles cleanly without stray unused imports. I also confirm QuoteMode lives in the same org.apache.commons.csv package, so it needs no qualified import.

I decide the test class should also live in package org.apache.commons.csv, matching the typical test suite layout, since it only relies on public members anyway.

I'm verifying that passing a null cast varargs to withHeaderComments correctly propagates through toStringArray to leave headerComments null, matching the expected assertNull check. Now I'm finalizing the full test file structure, including any needed setup annotations.

I'm also revisiting the newRecord=true variant with the same character to check which branch it triggers.
